bear.writtenAnchor: AI and cloud demand normalises faster than the current build-out assumes. Azure growth decelerates from the 43% posted in the June 2026 quarter toward the rate of the broader commercial base, Windows OEM, devices and Xbox keep shrinking, and revenue growth settles near the weakest year in the filed decade (6.9% in FY2023). The enormous capital programme — capex of $115.9bn in FY2026 against $34.3bn of depreciation — lands in the cost base as depreciation catches up, so operating margin gives back the recent gains and runs below the ten-year median rather than at the FY2026 peak of 46.8%. New capital earns roughly the discount rate: filed ROIC has already fallen from 94.0% in FY2018 to 26.0% in FY2026 as invested capital scaled, and the five-year incremental return of 17.3% compresses further in a capital-heavy AI regime. Rising stock-based compensation outpaces repurchases and share count drifts up slightly.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: Set at the bottom of the filed single-year range (6.9% in FY2023), reflecting a demand normalisation in which the declining More Personal Computing lines (Windows OEM and devices down 7%, Xbox content down 10% in the June 2026 quarter) weigh on a decelerating cloud base.

operatingMargin.text: Below the 41.7% median and well below the 46.8% current level (H:margin), the level that would follow if depreciation on the AI fleet — D&A rose from $22.0bn to $34.3bn in one year against $115.9bn of capex (H:capex) — outruns the revenue it supports.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Net investment (capex less D&A) over revenue has a filed median of 6.2%; with slow growth the bear spends only slightly above that median rather than the 24.6% implied by FY2026's $115.9bn capex against $34.3bn D&A.

returnOnNewInvestment.text: Below the 17.3% five-year incremental return on new capital and far below any filed full-year ROIC, extending the decline from 67.1% in FY2021 to 26.0% in FY2026 as the capital-heavy AI estate dilutes returns (H:returns, H:capex). Allowed to sit near the discount rate in the downside case.

shareCount.text: Slight dilution: stock-based compensation has risen every year on file, to $12.4bn in FY2026, and in a weaker cash case repurchases (part of the $10.2bn of dividends and buybacks in the June 2026 quarter) no longer fully offset it. (1.02× today's diluted count)

base.writtenAnchor: Microsoft compounds off a very large base at a rate between its ten-year CAGR (14.7%) and the slowest year on file. Commercial remaining performance obligation of $684bn at FY2026 year-end, up from $375bn a year earlier, plus Microsoft 365 Copilot at over 30 million paid seats and Azure crossing $100bn of annual revenue, underpin mid-teens growth that fades as the backlog converts. Operating margin holds close to the FY2026 level of 46.8% — mix shifts toward capital-intensive cloud and AI infrastructure, which carries more depreciation, but software and M365 scale offsets it — so the base sits just below the peak at 45.5%. Returns on new capital stay well above the cost of capital but far below the asset-light history: 18% is near the trailing five-year incremental return of 17.3% and well under the 26.0% FY2026 ROIC. Net reinvestment stays elevated versus the 6.2% median of capex less depreciation as data-centre spend continues, and steady repurchases shrink the share count modestly.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: Between the filed ten-year CAGR of 14.7% and the slow years, reflecting 18% FY2026 growth and commercial RPO of $684bn (up from $375bn) converting over several years while the base grows larger and Windows/Xbox lines shrink.

operatingMargin.text: A touch below the FY2026 record of 46.8% and above the 45.6% of FY2025 (H:margin); the June quarter ran at 45.1% operating margin ($40.6bn on $90.0bn, E1), and rising AI depreciation (H:capex) argues against assuming further expansion.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: FY2026 net investment was $81.6bn of capex less D&A on $331.8bn of revenue, about 24.6%, against a filed median of 6.2%; the base assumes the AI build moderates to a level well above history but well below the FY2026 peak.

returnOnNewInvestment.text: Close to the filed five-year incremental return on new capital of 17.3% and comfortably below the FY2026 ROIC of 26.0%; it sits above the base terminal return of 12.0% (9.0% discount rate plus the 3.0-point wide-moat credit).

shareCount.text: Modest net shrinkage: Microsoft returned $10.2bn in dividends and repurchases in each of the last two reported quarters, which offsets stock-based compensation of $12.4bn in FY2026 and leaves a small annual reduction. (0.98× today's diluted count)

bull.writtenAnchor: The agentic-computing cycle keeps Microsoft's growth at the top of its filed range. Revenue grew 18% in FY2026 and 17.7% in the June quarter, Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 27% to $59.3bn, Azure grew 43%, and the AI business passed a $37bn run rate up 123% year over year; commercial RPO up 84% to $678bn gives multi-year visibility. Growth holds at 16% for five years. The AI stack proves high-margin as utilisation of the FY2024–FY2026 capex wave rises, pushing operating margin above the FY2026 record to 48%. New capital earns 22% after tax — above the recent five-year incremental return of 17.3% but still below the 26.0% ROIC Microsoft actually filed in FY2026 — and strong free cash flow (operating cash flow $182.9bn in FY2026) funds both the build-out and continued repurchases, lowering the share count.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: Near the top of the filed single-year range (18.0%) and just above the ten-year CAGR of 14.7%, supported by FY2026 revenue growth of 18%, Azure up 43% and commercial RPO up 84% to $678bn at quarter-end.

operatingMargin.text: Slightly above the FY2026 record of 46.8%, extending the unbroken ten-year climb from 30.1%, as utilisation of the installed AI capacity rises; operating income grew 21% in FY2026 against 18% revenue growth, showing continued leverage.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Elevated against the 6.2% median because faster growth requires continued capacity, but below the roughly 24.6% FY2026 peak as D&A catches up with capex (D&A rose from $22.0bn to $34.3bn) and the fleet is utilised against the $678bn contracted backlog (H:capex, H:revenue, E1).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: Above the five-year incremental return of 17.3% but still below the 26.0% ROIC Microsoft actually filed in FY2026, and far below 1.5 times the best filed return; it clears the bull terminal return of 13.5% (9.0% plus 3.0 wide-moat points plus the 1.5 bull point).

shareCount.text: Operating cash flow reached $182.9bn in FY2026 against $12.4bn of stock-based compensation; with capex funded internally, the $10.2bn-per-quarter shareholder return can tilt further to repurchases and shrink the diluted count faster. (0.95× today's diluted count)

moatAnchor.text: Switching costs reinforced by intangible assets and efficient scale: Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, Dynamics 365 and Azure are embedded in customer operations, shown by commercial remaining performance obligation of $684bn at FY2026 year-end (up from $73bn in FY2018) and over 30 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats, while global data-centre scale supports a $100bn-plus Azure business. The filed returns support the credit: ROIC has been 26.0% or higher in every year since FY2018, peaking at 94.0%, far above the 9.0% discount rate, so a 12.0% terminal return sits well below any return the company has filed.

constantsAnchor.text: No company-specific effective tax disclosure was supplied, so the general US federal statutory rate of 21.0% is used — the same rate used to compute NOPAT in the filed return history. The stress margin of 36% is below both the current margin of 46.8% and the ten-year median of 41.7%, and sits between the FY2019 (34.1%) and FY2020 (37.0%) filed levels.

base.writtenAnchor: Microsoft compounds off a very large base at a rate between its ten-year CAGR (14.7%) and the slowest year on file. Commercial remaining performance obligation of $684bn at FY2026 year-end, up from $375bn a year earlier, plus Microsoft 365 Copilot at over 30 million paid seats and Azure crossing $100bn of annual revenue, underpin mid-teens growth that fades as the backlog converts. Operating margin holds close to the FY2026 level of 46.8% — mix shifts toward capital-intensive cloud and AI infrastructure, which carries more depreciation, but software and M365 scale offsets it — so the base sits just below the peak at 45.5%. Returns on new capital stay well above the cost of capital but far below the asset-light history: 18% is near the trailing five-year incremental return of 17.3% and well under the 26.0% FY2026 ROIC. Net reinvestment stays elevated versus the 6.2% median of capex less depreciation as data-centre spend continues, and steady repurchases shrink the share count modestly.

bull.writtenAnchor: The agentic-computing cycle keeps Microsoft's growth at the top of its filed range. Revenue grew 18% in FY2026 and 17.7% in the June quarter, Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 27% to $59.3bn, Azure grew 43%, and the AI business passed a $37bn run rate up 123% year over year; commercial RPO up 84% to $678bn gives multi-year visibility. Growth holds at 16% for five years. The AI stack proves high-margin as utilisation of the FY2024–FY2026 capex wave rises, pushing operating margin above the FY2026 record to 48%. New capital earns 22% after tax — above the recent five-year incremental return of 17.3% but still below the 26.0% ROIC Microsoft actually filed in FY2026 — and strong free cash flow (operating cash flow $182.9bn in FY2026) funds both the build-out and continued repurchases, lowering the share count.

narrative.text: Microsoft Corporation, a technology company, develops and supports a portfolio of technology solutions for individuals and businesses worldwide. Its products include operating systems, server applications, business solution applications, software development tools, desktop and server management tools, and video games; and devices, such as PCs, tablets, gaming and entertainment consoles, other intelligent devices, and related accessories. The company's Productivity and Business Processes segment offers Microsoft 365 Commercial, Enterprise Mobility + Security, Power BI, Exchange, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Security and Compliance, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Windows Commercial on-premises and Office licensed on-premises. This segment also provides Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services; LinkedIn, including talent solutions, marketing solutions, subscriptions, and sales solutions; Dynamics 365, a set of cloud-based applications; and on-premises ERP and CRM applications. Its Intelligent Cloud segment offers server products and cloud services; cloud and AI consumption-based services, GitHub cloud services, health and life sciences cloud services, as well as virtual desktop offerings, and other cloud services; SQL Server, Windows Server, Visual Studio, System Center, and related client access licenses; and enterprise support services, industry solutions, Microsoft partner network, and learning experience. The company's More Personal Computing segment provides Windows OEM licensing and devices comprising Surface and PC accessories; XBOX hardware, and XBOX first- and third-party content and services; XBOX Game Pass and other subscriptions; XBOX Cloud Gaming, advertising, and other cloud services; and search advertising consisting of Bing, Copilot, Microsoft News, Microsoft Edge, and third-party affiliates. It sells its products through partners and retail networks. The company was founded in 1975 and is headquartered in Redmond, Washington.
